U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors Industrial Mandate & Operating Envelope

Oklo’s Aurora SFR targets high burnup at 400–650 °C and 100–200 dpa, leveraging metallic fuel’s high fissile density.

Company Mandate
15–75 MWe
Select fuel–cladding system for Oklo’s pool-type Aurora SFR under NUREG-2246 & NUREG/CR-7305.
Why Metallic Fuel
~14.4 gHM/cm³
16.0–16.2 g/cm³ alloy (20 °C; 15.5 at 650 °C) → ~50% higher HM density than UO2/MOX (~9.7 gHM/cm³), plus passive feedback.
Core Operating Envelope
≤ 650 °C • 100–200 dpa
Peak cladding temperature ≤ 650 °C, fast neutron dose 100–200 dpa, legacy EBR-II/FFTF basis.

A3F at INL: PDSA approved Nov 2025; EBR-II recycled fuel pathway for initial Aurora core loading.

Licensing Basis: NRC Aurora Fuel Qualification Report aligned with NUREG-2246 & NUREG/CR-7305.

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors Reference Fuel Pin Architecture

A 75% smeared-density U-10Zr slug with liquid Na bond and HT9 cladding decouples swelling from early mechanical stress.

NUREG/CR-7305 Reference Pin
Fuel / Bond / CladdingU-10wt%Zr / Liquid Na / HT9
Fuel OD / Cladding OD5.0 mm / 6.9 mm (0.6 mm wall)
Smeared Density75% max
Plenum-to-Fuel Ratio1.4× fuel volume
BOL Peak LHGR / Burnup40–55 kW/m / 10 at% envelope
  • Thermal Design Role: Liquid Na bond minimizes BOL fuel ΔT; 75% smear density leaves space for early swelling.
  • Interface Limit: Steady-state PICT capped at 650 °C to limit creep, FCCI, and liquefaction.

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors U-10Zr Metallurgy & Phase Behavior

Adding 10 wt% Zr raises the solidus well above 1200 °C and stabilizes BCC γ-phase, despite complex solid-state transitions.

Solidus & Liquidus: ~1248 °C solidus (1521 K) / ~1355–1360 °C liquidus (vs 1135 °C pure U) • cp = 248 J/(kg·K)
  • Role of 10 wt% Zr: Raises solidus to ~1248 °C (lowest U–Zr solidus >1100 °C in Zr-depleted zone) and slows U–Fe interdiffusion.
  • Isotropy Advantage: High-temperature γ-BCC phase resists anisotropic irradiation growth seen in orthorhombic α-U.

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors Fabrication, Na-Bonding & Joining

Injection casting, Na-bond inspection, and HT9 end-cap welding with PWHT govern as-built pin integrity.

STEP 01 • SLUG CASTING
Vacuum injection casting in quartz molds (EBR-II heritage) vs hot extrusion to avoid mold waste.
STEP 02 • HT9 & Na-BONDING
VIM → extrusion → cold drawing (norm. ~1050 °C + temp. ~750 °C); molten Na centrifuged & UT-inspected against voids.
STEP 03 • END-CAP JOINING
GTAW/TIG or RPW welding; PWHT required in HT9 to temper hard, brittle martensite in HAZ.

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors In-Pile Fuel Evolution: Swelling, FGR & Zr Migration

Interconnected gas porosity vents ~70–80% of fission gas at ~30% swelling, while thermal gradients drive radial Zr redistribution.

A Early Gas Swelling: Rapid expansion (~30–33% vol.) closes the initial gap without excessive FCMI.
B Fission Gas Release (FGR): Interconnected porosity forms and vents ~70–80% of fission gas into the plenum.
C Na Infiltration: Liquid Na enters open pores—preserving thermal conductivity, but creating fast transport paths for lanthanides.
D Radial Zr Redistribution: Thermal gradient pushes Zr to hot center (γ-phase) and outer rim, leaving a Zr-depleted mid-radius zone.

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors Fuel-Cladding Chemical Interaction (FCCI) & Eutectic

Lanthanides migrate via Na-filled pores to thin HT9 cladding and risk U–Fe eutectic liquefaction above ~725 °C.

CRITICAL INTERFACE DEGRADATION: Lanthanide FCCI Wastage + U–Fe Eutectic Liquefaction EUTECTIC THRESHOLD ~725 °C
01 • Transport Driver
Lanthanide Attack: Fission-product lanthanides (Nd, Ce, La, Pr) migrate to the cladding ID and form brittle Ln–Fe intermetallics.
02 • Structural Degradation
Cladding Wastage: Cr/Fe outward interdiffusion leaves a weak, thinned load-bearing wall (limiting lifetime at T > 600 °C).
03 • Transient Breach
Eutectic Liquefaction: U6Fe and UFe2 form a low-melting U–Fe eutectic at ~725 °C, causing rapid cladding breach during transients.

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors Cladding Metallurgy: FCC Austenitics vs BCC F/M (HT9)

BCC HT9 suppresses void swelling (<2% at 200 dpa) via low dislocation bias, trading off low-T DBTT shift and >650 °C creep limits.

Criterion FCC Austenitics (316SS / D9) BCC F/M HT9 (Baseline)
Microstructure & Chemistry Face-centered cubic (316SS / D9) austenitic matrix. Fe-12Cr-1Mo-0.5W-0.5Ni-0.3V-0.2C tempered martensite.
Void Swelling (@ 200 dpa) High dislocation bias drives steep swelling (~1%/dpa) after incubation. <2% at 200 dpa (400–420 °C) via high lath sink density.
Low-T Embrittlement No low-temperature DBTT shift. Below ~400 °C (T < 0.4 Tm), hardening + α′ (>9 wt% Cr) drive ΔDBTT ≈ +155 °C, saturating by 5–10 dpa.
High-T Creep & FCCI High early thermal creep strength, but Ni leaching worsens FCCI. Creep ceiling above 600–650 °C (~60 MPa at 105 h / 600 °C).
FCC CAP: ~10 at% BU (Void Swelling)
HT9 WINDOW: 400–650 °C (<2% Swelling)

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors Legacy Irradiation Database (EBR-II & FFTF)

Over 1,260 U-10Zr/HT9 pins tested to 14–20 at% burnup prove steady-state reliability and bound failure thresholds.

01 • US Heritage EBR-II + FFTF
>130,000 Pins
Includes >13,600 U–Zr / U–Pu–Zr pins
02 • Qualified NUREG/CR-7305
1,262 Pins
404 EBR-II + 858 FFTF in HT9 cladding
03 • Peak Burnup ~200 GWd/MTHM
Up to ~20 at%
~20 at% in EBR-II • 14.3 at% in FFTF
04 • Breach Limit EBR-II X447
660 °C PICT
FCCI + creep limit → 650 °C PICT cap
  • Massive US Heritage: NUREG/CR-7305 qualifies 1,262 U-10Zr/HT9 rods across 404 EBR-II and 858 FFTF tests.
  • Strain Reliability: Zero strain-induced breaches for ≤ 75% smear density below 17 at% burnup (370–615 °C).
  • Failure Boundary: Breaches in EBR-II X447 occurred at 660 °C at top of fuel column (z/L ≈ 1.0) due to combined FCCI thinning and thermal creep.

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors Advanced Mitigation Levers

Four material engineering strategies target FCCI elimination, sodium-bond waste, and the 650 °C HT9 creep limit.

LEVER 01 Interface Barrier

Internal Anti-FCCI Barriers

Co-extruded Zr liner or thin V/Cr/TiN inner coating physically blocks Ln–Fe and U–Fe interdiffusion.

LEVER 02 Matrix Chemistry

Fuel Dopants (Pd, Sn, Sb)

Small additions bind lanthanides inside the U–Zr slug as stable intermetallics (Pd–Ln, Sn–Ln).

LEVER 03 Pin Geometry

Annular He-Bonded (55% Smear)

Eliminates liquid Na bond (removes fast Ln paths & pyrophoric Na disposal issues; tighter gap tolerance).

LEVER 04 Advanced Cladding

9Cr-ODS Cladding Fe-9Cr-2W-0.2Ti-0.35Y2O3

1–3 nm Y–Ti–O nano-oxides suppress α′ brittleness, trap He, and raise creep limit to ~700 °C (requires solid-state PRW weld).

Synthesized from Xie et al. (2018), Yao et al. (2023), Seki et al. (2004), and IAEA (2013).

Selecting a metallic fuel architecture requires balancing licensing maturity against temperature margin and back-end waste.

Commercial Baseline 		<2% swelling at 200 dpa; 1,262-pin NRC database; high k High-burnup FCCI wastage; reactive Na-bond waste Creep >650 °C; U–Fe eutectic (725 °C)
U-10Zr (Na+Liner/Pd) / HT9
Stage 1 Target 		Cuts FCCI wastage & extends burnup using qualified HT9 tube Extra fabrication/coating cost; unaddressed HT9 creep ceiling HT9 thermal creep >650 °C; liner bonding QA
Annular U-10Zr (He) / 9Cr-ODS
Stage 2 Target 		No reactive Na waste; creep to ~700 °C; low α′ risk Lower gap kHe; expensive PM/MA tubing; low TRL PRW end-cap weld qual.; tight gap tolerances
MOX / 15-15Ti
External Benchmark 		Mature oxide/LWR fabrication & European LFR/SFR heritage 8–10× lower k; lower fissile density; no Na-bond synergy Centerline T margin; 15-15Ti swelling >120 dpa
Commercial Baseline

U-10Zr (Na) / HT9

1,262-pin NUREG/CR-7305 licensing database; capped by HT9 thermal creep >650 °C & U–Fe eutectic (725 °C).

Stage 1 Target

Na + Liner / Pd in HT9

Cuts Ln–Fe FCCI wastage inside qualified HT9 tubes (~10–14 at% BU, PICT ≤620 °C) for near-term launch.

Stage 2 Target

Annular He / 9Cr-ODS

Eliminates pyrophoric Na-bond waste and extends creep ceiling to ~700 °C (>15 at% BU; requires PRW).

Trade-off grounded in NUREG/CR-7305, PNNL-35642, IAEA-TECDOC-1689, and Xie et al. (2018).

U-10Zr Metallic Fuel for Sodium Fast Reactors Selection, Engineering Opinion & Limitations

A two-stage deployment strategy pairs immediate NRC licensability with next-generation high-temperature performance.

MY PROPOSAL 01 • Duplex PVD/ALD Inner Barrier

Replace thick co-extruded Zr-rind with an ultra-thin PVD/ALD duplex coating (Cr/V + Y2O3 or TiN ceramic diffusion barrier, analogous to ATF anti-eutectic barriers): suppresses both Ln wastage and 725 °C U–Fe liquefaction inside standard HT9 tubes.

MY PROPOSAL 02 • Recycled-Pd Doping in Annular Fuel

Valorize noble fission-product Pd recovered during EBR-II electrorefining (~1–2 wt% Pd addition) inside an annular He-bonded slug: traps lanthanides as stable PdLn / Pd2Ln intermetallics while eliminating pyrophoric Na-bond disposal.

HONEST BOTTLENECKS • Joining & Industrial Scale-Up

Fusion welding destroys 9Cr-ODS nano-oxides (Y2O3 coarsening): Stage 2 requires industrial qualification of solid-state PRW end-cap joining, lower PM/MA tubing cost, tight He-gap tolerances, and prototypic TREAT transient tests.
